text: It is narrated from Jabir that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) addressed the people, he would first praise and glorify Allah as He deserves, and then say: “Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray; and whomever Allah leads astray, none can guide. The best of speech is the Book of Allah.”

Ibn Umar narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Islam is built upon five pillars: bearing witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving zakat, performing the Hajj, and fasting in Ramadan.”

It is narrated from Anas (ibn Malik) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever has these three qualities will taste the sweetness of faith: loving Allah and His Messenger more than anything else; loving a person solely for the sake of Allah; and hating to return to disbelief after Allah has saved him from it, just as he would hate to be thrown into the Fire.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Faith has seventy-some branches. The highest of them is the saying ‘La ilaha illallah’ (There is no god but Allah), and the lowest is removing something harmful from the road. Modesty (haya) is also a branch of faith.”
Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to supplicate: “O Allah! I seek refuge in You from discord, from hypocrisy, and from bad character.”

It is narrated from Aisha that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “The one who memorizes and recites the Quran will be with the noble, honored angels in the presence of Allah. And the one who strives to recite the Quran regularly, even though it is difficult for him, will have a double reward.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, in this world and in the Hereafter. The prophets are brothers with one father and different mothers; their religion is one.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), speaking about Friday, said: “There is an hour in it such that if a Muslim happens upon it while praying and asks Allah for something, Allah will surely grant him what he asks.”
It is narrated from Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Repentance from a sin is to abandon the sin and never return to it again.”

It is narrated from Muadh ibn Jabal that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Beware of the three things that bring curses: relieving oneself near water sources, in the middle of the road, and in shaded places.”
It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “It is a right of Allah the Exalted upon every Muslim that he bathe once every seven days.”

Hanzala (ibn Rabi') al-Katib (who served as a scribe of revelation for the Prophet) narrates: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: “Whoever keeps up the five daily prayers, observing their bowings, prostrations, ablutions and times, and accepts that these five prayers are a true command from Allah, will enter Paradise.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The closest a servant comes to his Lord is when he is in prostration. So make abundant supplication (while prostrating).”
It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The most perfect of the believers in faith is the one who is best in character.”

topic: Good Character · The Heart and Deeds
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Allah does not look at your appearances or your wealth; rather, He looks at your hearts and your deeds.”

Wabisa ibn Ma'bad, of the tribe of Asad, narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: “… Goodness is that which brings peace to the heart and settles comfortably within; evil is that which unsettles the heart and leaves doubt within you, even if people give you a ruling (approving it).”

topic: Good Character · Loving for Allah's Sake
text: It is narrated from Abu Dharr that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The most virtuous of deeds is to love for the sake of Allah and to hate for the sake of Allah.”

Nu'man ibn Bashir narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “In their mutual love, mercy and compassion, the believers are like a single body: when one organ of it is ailing, the rest of the body shares its pain with sleeplessness and fever.”

It is narrated from Anas (ibn Malik) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Shamelessness disfigures whatever it is found in and whoever has it; modesty adorns whatever it is found in and whoever has it.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “A woman is married for four things: her wealth, her lineage, her beauty and her religion. Choose the one who is religious. (Otherwise) you will be reduced to poverty and want!”

It is narrated from Thawban that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “It is not permissible for anyone to look inside another person's house without permission. If he looks, it is as if he has entered (the house)...”
source: Tirmidhi, Salât, 148; Ahmad ibn Hanbal, V, 280

text: Abu al-Darda narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Indeed, on the Day of Resurrection you will be called by your names and the names of your fathers. So give (your children) good names.”

topic: Social Life · Communication Within the Family
text: Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “A believer should not harbor ill feelings toward his wife; for even if he dislikes some of her traits, he may be pleased with others.”

topic: Social Life · Women, the Mosque and Congregation
text: It is narrated from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from coming to the mosques of Allah.”

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Prophet (peace be upon him) say: “Allah the Exalted said: ‘When I test My servant through his two beloved ones (by taking his eyes) and he remains patient, I will give him Paradise in return for them.’”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “All of my community will enter Paradise, except the one who turns away!” Those present asked, “O Messenger of Allah, who is the one who turns away?” The Prophet (peace be upon him) replied, “Whoever obeys me will enter Paradise. Whoever disobeys me has turned away.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “I swear by Allah, in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, that any Jew or Christian of this community who hears of me and then dies without believing in what I have been sent with (the revelation) will surely be among the people of the Fire.”

topic: Faith · Learning and Teaching the Holy Quran
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that… the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Learn the Quran, recite it and teach it to others. The one who learns the Quran, recites it and acts upon it is like a vessel full of musk spreading its fragrance everywhere. And the one who learns the Quran but then lies down and sleeps (without reciting or teaching it) is like a vessel of musk whose mouth has been tied shut.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not trouble his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.”

topic: Faith · Self-Reckoning and Preparing for the Hereafter
text: It is narrated from Shaddad ibn Aws that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “The wise person is the one who holds himself to account and works for what comes after death. The helpless one is the one who follows his desires and then hopes (for forgiveness) from Allah.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The believer is like a green crop. The wind bends it (but does not break it), and when the wind calms down, it stands upright again. So it is with the believer: he too bends under trials and afflictions (but does not break). The disbeliever, however, is like a hard, rigid cypress tree, which Allah uproots and fells (all at once) whenever He wills.”
Ibn Umar narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “The hypocrite is like a bewildered sheep wavering between two flocks, going now to that flock, now to this one!”

It is narrated from Aisha that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Strive to do the deeds that you are able to sustain. Allah does not grow weary, but you will grow weary. The most beloved of deeds to Allah are those done consistently, even if they are few.”

It is narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib that the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to supplicate at the end of the witr prayer: “O Allah! I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and in Your pardon from Your punishment. I seek refuge in You from You (from every kind of punishment that may come from You). I cannot praise You as You deserve. You are as You have praised Yourself.”

topic: Worship · The Imam and the Muezzin
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The imam is a guarantor (for the prayers of those who follow him), and the muezzin is one who is entrusted (with the prayer times). O Allah! Grant success to the imams (in what they guarantee), and forgive the muezzins (for their possible shortcomings)!”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was placed in Paradise, and on it he was sent out of Paradise. And the Last Hour will take place on no day other than Friday.”

topic: Worship · Prayer and the First Reckoning
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The first thing for which a servant will be called to account (on the Day of Resurrection) is his prayer. If he has performed it completely, (all is well!) But if (his obligatory prayers) are not complete, Allah the Exalted will say: ‘Look at the voluntary prayers of My servant.’ If voluntary prayers are found, He will say: ‘Complete the obligatory ones with them.’”

topic: Worship · Ramadan Fasting and the Night of Power
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and hoping for its reward from Allah, his past sins will be forgiven. And whoever spends the Night of Power in worship out of faith and hoping for its reward from Allah, his past sins will be forgiven.”

Abu Dharr narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: “Be mindful of your responsibility toward Allah wherever you are! Follow a bad deed with a good one, so that it wipes it out. And treat people with good character!”

topic: Good Character · Provision for the Hereafter
text: Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr narrates: I heard from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Three things follow the deceased (to the grave); two return and one remains. His family, his wealth and his deeds follow him. His family and his wealth return, and his deeds remain.”

Amir heard from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “… Know that in the body there is a piece of flesh which, if it is sound (upright and well), the whole body is sound; and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Know that it is the heart.”

topic: Good Character · Doing Everything for Allah
text: It is narrated from Abu Umamah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever loves for the sake of Allah, hates for the sake of Allah, gives for the sake of Allah, and withholds (from evil) for the sake of Allah has perfected his faith.”

It is narrated from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The believer who mixes with people and bears patiently the harm they cause attains a greater reward than the believer who does not mix with people and does not bear patiently the harm they cause.”
source: Ibn Majah, Fiten 23; Ahmad ibn Hanbal, II, 44

text: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr narrates: The People of the Suffa were poor. The Prophet (peace be upon him) had said: “Whoever has food for two, let him host a third person; and whoever has food for four, let him host a fifth or a sixth!”

topic: Social Life · The Trials of a Person
text: Hudhayfah heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: “A person is tested through his family, his wealth, his own self, his child and his neighbor; fasting, prayer, charity, and enjoining good and forbidding evil are an expiation for (his shortcomings during) this testing.”

Abu Hurairah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “A previously married woman may not be married without her consent, and a virgin may not be married without her permission.” The Companions present asked, “O Messenger of Allah! How is a virgin's permission given?” He (peace be upon him) said, “By her remaining silent.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “Know your lineages so that you may maintain your ties of kinship. For keeping the ties of kinship alive strengthens love within the family, increases wealth and lengthens life.”
source: Tirmidhi, Birr, 49; Ahmad ibn Hanbal, II, 374

text: Anas ibn Malik narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “If a young person honors an elderly person because of his age, Allah will appoint for him someone who will honor him in his old age.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “The best house among (the houses of) the Muslims is a house in which there is an orphan who is treated well. And the worst house among the Muslims is a house in which there is an orphan who is treated badly.”

topic: Social Life · Supplication When Visiting the Sick
text: It is narrated from Aisha that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) visited a sick person, he would say: “O Lord of mankind! Remove the hardship of the illness! Heal him, for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing. Grant a healing that leaves no trace of illness behind!”
